finding.claim: /logo SSRF: substring check strings.Contains(raw, "example.io") is not a host check, so any URL containing 'example.io' anywhere (e.g. http://example.io.attacker.test/ or http://169.254.169.254/?example.io) is fetched and the response is returned to the caller.
finding.source: main.go:31 r.FormValue("logo") (unauthenticated, route registered at main.go:43)
finding.sink: main.go:36 http.Get(raw); response copied back at main.go:38 io.Copy(w, resp.Body)

trace.note: strings.Contains substring test, not host equality; no private/link-local IP blocking
response body streamed to attacker (full-read SSRF)

finding.guards_checked: Substring check at main.go:32 only (insufficient). No scheme allowlist beyond Go client http/https, no host allowlist, no IP-range block, no response size limit.

verdict.guard_found: none. The only check is the substring test at main.go:32 (strings.Contains(raw, "example.io")), which does not close the finding. No host allowlist, IP-range block, or scheme restriction exists on the path to the sink at main.go:36.
verdict.reason: main.go:31 takes the unauthenticated `logo` form value, main.go:32 only checks for the substring "example.io", and main.go:36 passes it straight to http.Get with the default client, whose body is copied back to the caller at main.go:38 (route registered without auth at main.go:43).

finding.claim: /logo follows redirects (DefaultClient, no CheckRedirect), so a host that passes the weak check can 302 the server to internal or metadata addresses. /cdn at main.go:12/24 disables redirects; /logo does not.
finding.sink: main.go:36 http.Get(raw) follows up to 10 redirects

redirect target body returned to attacker

finding.guards_checked: None on redirects at /logo. Contrast: noRedirect defined at main.go:12 and applied only in cdn() at main.go:24. /cdn is SAFE (exact trusted-host check main.go:20, redirects blocked).

verdict.guard_found: None closing. The only check on the /logo path is strings.Contains(raw, "example.io") at main.go:32, which is a substring match and does not close the finding. No redirect restriction exists on the DefaultClient call at main.go:36. Contrast: /cdn (main.go:24-25) uses noRedirect and an exact hostname map lookup (main.go:20), so it is safe.
verdict.reason: main.go:31 takes the unauthenticated `logo` parameter, main.go:32 only checks that it contains "example.io" (substring, not a hostname match), and main.go:36 calls http.Get with the default client, which follows redirects, and main.go:38 returns the response body to the caller. The trace is accurate. The attacker can also skip the redirect entirely by passing an internal URL with "example.io" in its query string, so the SSRF is at least as strong as the candidate describes.
